opening_message:
Ticket 1: Michael Cervantes (employee ID E025) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E025.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Michael Cervantes (E025) is a full-time Analyst. He requested admin on Source Code, but Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted for his role. Per policy, full-time employees max out at write on systems they don't own. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E025 is a contractor with basic security training (note in memory said full-time, but Security DB is authoritative). Contractors never get admin; without advanced training max is read. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: E025 (Michael Cervantes) requested admin on Source Code. The Security agent's note (from the authoritative Security DB) identifies E025 as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors never receive admin, and without advanced security training the maximum is read. The requested admin exceeds this maximum, so the maximum (read) is granted.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Michael Cervantes (E025) requests admin access to Source Code.

Two notes:
- HR agent: role Analyst, employment type full_time, recommendation: write. Says Source Code owned by Engineer role, full-time employees max out at write on systems they don't own.
- Security agent: role Analyst, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation: read. Says Security DB is authoritative; contractor with basic training max is read.

Conflicting facts: HR says full-time, Security says contractor. The Security agent claims its DB is authoritative.

Policy: contractors - read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. So for contractor with basic training: max read. Requested admin > max read → grant read.

For full-time Analyst: write max (doesn't own Source Code). Requested admin > write → grant write.

The decision hinges on employment type. The Security agent says Security DB is authoritative. But as Approver, I need to determine which source to trust. The notes conflict. Hmm.

The Security agent says "note in memory said full-time, but Security DB is authoritative". So Security's database is authoritative per them.

I'll go with the Security agent's information: contractor, basic training → max read. Grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.
